utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic, also known as "Vlado."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we call the witness, may I simply draw your attention to the response from the Registrar to our request concerning the possible provision of transcripts in Croatian to the Defence. I'm afraid, as you may have seen, the response is negative for reasons which are well set out in the statement by the Registrar. However, as we also had already pointed out in our request to the Registrar, I think the Defence counsel, and this is, again, stressed by the Registrar, Defence counsel are welcome to consult the audio tapes where you can hear the original of what was said in Croatian in court, so just to check what was said, if you have a doubt in your mind or if you don't want to confine yourselves to the English transcript. We also received a response regarding the medical examination of one of the accused. I imagine the relevant Defence counsel, Mr. Krajina, has also received that document. We may now move on to our closed session. Mr. Moskowitz, do you think it is necessary to go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, it will be necessary only during a certain part of the video where he will identify his house and some surrounding areas around his house, but I think after that, we don't need to be in closed session. We have a couple of preliminary questions that I would like to ask that will not need to be in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Right. So we are now in open session, and you'll let us know when you request that we should go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yesterday, you talked about seeing soldiers with patches, and I would, at the start of this session, show you some exhibits to see if you can identify any of those patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I would ask the usher first to show the witness previously admitted Exhibits 103 and 104.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you recognise that Exhibit 103?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. I know this and I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see that on some of the soldiers you saw on the 16th of April and on the days following while you were in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The next exhibit, 104, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Would you look at Exhibit 104 and tell us if that looks familiar to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this insignia on certain soldiers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And that would be during the period you described yesterday, April 16th, 1993 and on the days following?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could we also show the witness previously admitted Exhibit 45?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 45, now having been placed on the ELMO, is that familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is similar to the insignia I saw, but I'm not certain whether this was written, "Military Police," and I'm not sure about this checkerboard symbol. I recall seeing the Jokers, but I don't know in which shape or form.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Having recalled seeing a patch similar, but not exactly like that, again, are we talking about the time period of April 16, 1993 and the days following while you were in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I have one more exhibit, which is in a new one, that I would like to tender at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 118.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 118?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 118 has now been placed on the ELMO next to you. Could you look at that and identify that, if you can, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. This is also an insignia I saw certain soldiers wear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That, again, would be during the time period we already mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you for that. You also testified yesterday about the Bungalow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask the usher, again, I'm sorry, to display this exhibit to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 119.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can you identify Exhibit 119, having now been placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is the Bungalow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Is this the same Bungalow you mentioned yesterday in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, behind you is a blow-up of the village of Ahmici. Could you turn around and look at that for us, please? Does that look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. This is a map of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you see in the centre of that map a large white area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: You mean this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I want you to think back to before the attack in 1993. Was there a large white area like that in Ahmici in the days and years and months before April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No. It did not exist. This was some kind of a mound and there was a depression there, and then later on, it was all levelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When you say "later on it was all levelled," do you mean after April 16, 1993, at some point it was all levelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. After April of 1993, it was levelled and turned into a parking lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you describe what kind of road or path went through that area before April 1993 and the terrain that was there before April 1993? You can use your pointer to help you illustrate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Earlier, there was a road there, too, which was used, but if we walked on foot, we would use a shortcut, because that path was much closer, rather than go all the way around here. So there was a path of sorts. And on this kind of mound that used to be there, we used to play there because it was good for playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, also I think yesterday you indicated that you may have seen someone who resembled Dario Kordic. Where was that person, if you can recall, that you saw, using, again, your pointer to demonstrate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: There was a house there, and I noticed that the jeep was coming from this direction. I saw the driver and there was a man sitting next to him. The jeep went there, and then it turned around and came back. I did not know who it was. I could not guess. But after awhile, I saw posters, pictures of Dario Kordic which were posted there, and then I thought that maybe Dario Kordic was in this jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, before coming into court today, have you had an opportunity to view a videotape, actually, two separate videotapes, but let's focus on the first one. Did you have an opportunity to view a videotape that showed various scenes in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Are you able to, at this time, recollecting that videotape as best you can, demonstrate for the Court the route that you feel the photographer took as he or she videotaped Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It went along the main road and past somewhere down here. I don't know how far down it went. I believe it may have turned around here and then slowly, and I noted it was slowly, it started coming back, very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did the photographer continue to travel down that main road, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. I think that it went all the way up here, and I don't know whether, on the second videotape, they turned here or whether that was still part of the first video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I'm going to ask, with the permission of the Court, for the first videotape to be played and, from time to time, ask that it be stopped so that the witness will have time to show where he feels the photographer was and the direction or angle of the shots so that we can get our bearings. It may be that this is an appropriate time, at least for the first part of this videotape, to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We'll go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can you show us, by using your pointer and pointing to the large blow-up, what you think the point of you is of this particular video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It is right here on the main road, between Sakib's house and Mehmed's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And what does this particular video shot show?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It shows the house -- I think his name was Suljo, Sakib's son, that is the first house you can see on the screen, that is white with big, black clouds of smoke coming from the windows. Behind it is Fehim's house, the son of Hilmija. Behind it comes Hilmija's house. Then a little to the right is Fikro and Sakib's house, and you can also see the minaret which is the minaret of the mosque. Also, a little bit to the right of this white house, from which this black smoke is coming, you can see a bit of asphalt, a kind of road that led to the village, and that is this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Then in this video would it be right to say that the Sakib house is immediately to the left, we haven't quite reached it yet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. Sakib's house is to the left, not far from this building material that we can see on the fence. After that comes Hakib's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So this would be Sakib's house coming into view now, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, this is Sakib's house. Behind it, what we just saw, was a kind of workshop, a carpenter's workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And are we now coming up to the road that leads into the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. Just behind this fence we will see the road. Here it is, the road leading to the village, entering the village. This big house is Radzo Pezer's house. Further up again we can see the mosque and the minaret, and another big house opposite the mosque, which is Kasim's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We can proceed and maybe stop as we get a view down the main road, or down the road into the village, that would be useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How about here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Anything new that you want to point out on this shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: From here we again see the road entering the village, and from here we can see all the houses that I have already pointed out, Suljo, Fehim's, Vehbija's, the mosque and the other houses that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now we're proceeding down the main road towards Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, we're going down the main road in the direction of Vitez. This is Redzo's stable that we're losing from sight, then comes Vidovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recognise that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it. This is also a Muslim house, but I don't know exactly the name of the owner, but it is next to some timber that didn't used to be there before. It is right here. And this house is this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you're pointing now on the exhibit of the blow-up of Ahmici, and near your pointer there seems to be a white area next to the main road. Do you know what that white area is or was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. Before there was nothing, it was the entrance to a shop, but now some building material is stored there, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Was that place called the Ogrjev by local people in Ahmici? You're familiar with that, Ogrjev?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No. This didn't exist before. It was built after the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And the house depicted in this video you believe is next to that white area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, it is this house, this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Still continuing down the main road there's a --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. We're going along the main road towards Vitez, and now towards the other side. It is showing these other houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please? Can we back up just for a second if we might? Back up to the previous shot of those two houses. Right there. Yes. Do you know those two houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. These two houses. They are these two houses, as I already mentioned, on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know who those houses belong to, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think that Suhreta lived in one of the two houses, and I don't know who lived in the other one. I think it was her sister or another relative who lived in the house next door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please, so we can get it in focus maybe a couple of frames. Good. Not so good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, do you have any idea where this was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I would like to ask if we could perhaps go back a little --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: -- I think the witness means.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think it is between this house and this house. Between these two houses. I think it is Zemko's house -- we've lost it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We need to go ahead to that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. You can just see the corner of the house on the screen. It is this house, Zemko's house. And next to it was Azra's house. We still can't see it on the monitor. Behind this haystack and behind the stable was Zemko's house. And behind Zemko's house you can see another house, which is this house here. It is this house, which was behind Zemko's house. And the body that we see and the path -- one may perhaps notice on the blow-up this path. You can see it on this aerial photograph, that there is a kind of path here. It's very faint.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we back up a little bit so we can get a close-up of the object in the centre of the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That's good. I think that's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you think that's a human body or is it an animal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is certainly a human body. It is a woman. You can see the head and the hair, you can see the hands and the legs. You can even see that she's wearing some sort of shoes on her feet. You can even see an ear and a nose on her head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can you recognise who this person is, or was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No, I cannot recognise it because I can't see the face. It could have been one of the inhabitants of the surrounding houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Are we still proceeding towards Vitez looking in a particular direction, or can you tell here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. No. We're still going towards Vitez. This is Dubravica, at the cross-roads. This is where --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we stop here, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: -- where the turning point is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The film jumps around a little bit. The previous section you recall is the Dubravica area right here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Can we stop there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. What do you see here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This, I think, quite a long time ago, maybe 20 years ago, this big building used to be, I think, a school, and now something was being made there, manufactured there. It was no longer a school. The school I went to was not far from here. This was the main road going towards Ahmici, Santici and then further on, and this was a road leading to Zenica. Turning off from this road was a road going to Zenica. Perhaps to the right one could see the edge of the road turning slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: This road to Zenica was the mountain road to Zenica, the Vjetrenica road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was the road via Vjetrenica. It is quite a high hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Here you can see the road turning off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we stop here for a moment. If you could orient us now on this video, tell us where you think we are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is viewed from the main road. The personnel carrier is partly on the road and partly on the grass bank. This is Sakib's house, which was at the very point where the road branches off for Ahmici. The small house that you can see to the right at the edge of the monitor, with some bricks and building blocks, is Mehmed's house, which was destroyed in October and it is actually situated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we stop there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know who this person is being carried out on the stretcher?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: In my opinion, this could be Merdanka, Sakib's wife who lived in Sakib's house. It could be a woman. You can see that she's rather fat and she has breasts, and she could be wearing pyjamas. I think it could be her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: But you don't know for certain who that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No, I don't know for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. Is it possible to identify that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you have any sense of where this was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This could be -- you can see a part of a small car, rather the lights, and this open door reminds me of the door of Zijad's garage, which was right of the road. He died, yes. This is this other house on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now we're panning back, and maybe this will give us more -- no, go ahead. Go forward, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: As the camera pans back, there will be more information. You can go at a faster speed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is not the garage that I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you have any idea where it is now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Could we go back a little, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Perhaps we can stop there. This is here, between these houses, close to the body that was lying on the road that was shown a moment ago, because a moment ago, we saw this big house which was behind, with the bricks and with the roof. And this small garage, and this, actually, to the right, I think, is a stable made out of blocks, and I think that is here. And this is the little path that led from Zemko's house to Azra's house. You would pass between the stable, the garage. And in between was the path going towards Azra's house which was right behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: May we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It's a big house, this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The one facing us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think perhaps behind the fence we can see this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Perhaps we can proceed at normal speed now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The corner that we saw a moment ago next to the tank, that was Zemko's house. This edge of the wall that we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you. You also talked about yesterday being picked up by UNPROFOR. And I would ask at this time before we turn the lights back on -- perhaps that's too late to request -- to play the second part of this video, and again, Witness G, if you could narrate for us, this is quite a bit shorter, and tell us what we're viewing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: As I have already said, as I said yesterday, I left this house here. Actually, I noticed from that house that UNPROFOR was somewhere here in Pirici, and I saw them moving in this direction, reaching this road and going down towards the mosque, past the mosque, and then it stopped somewhere here. One of them stopped next to Hadzija's house, one PC, and another one was right close by, and the other three or four stopped here next to Sakib's house, along the main road. As I said yesterday, when I saw them stopping there and coming out and looking around and taking photographs of I don't know what, I slowly got out of the house and headed along this road towards them to call out to them or do something like that. And so I went slowly, because I could only walk on one leg. At times I would rely on the other one with my toes, because I didn't dare lean on it fully. And holding on to a fence, I limped along slowly and reached Hidjet's house, and from there I still couldn't see them. So I went on, I passed Hidjet's house and reached roughly this point, this clearing here, and from there I could see them. They were, as I said already, near Hadzija's house and near Sakib's house, and there was another PC here. The others were on the main road. And from there I waved my hand and I called out to them. And when I said, "Come on, help me," they heard me and turned around. I called out another one or two times, and then lay down in the grass, because I was afraid that somebody from Papic's house or anyone else might see me. And as I was lying in the grass, I heard the PCs start but I thought they were leaving, because I couldn't see where they were going and I thought they were going to leave, thinking that perhaps this was some sort of ambush, and already I was thinking which house I should go to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Witness G, could I interrupt you for a moment? Could I direct your attention to the video in front of you, and if we can play that, perhaps that will illustrate your testimony more vividly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Is that the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. The right-hand side was the school, and they were there. They were going from the upper part and they were at the mosque already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If we could stop there for a moment, just so that we can get our bearings. Could you show us on the aerial map the point of view of this particular shot, if you can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It was filmed from here. You can see Hadzija's house a little bit. Then you can see the school yard, a part of it, over on the other side. And here was the mosque, which, by now, had been destroyed. This was the eighth day. This was where the bus, the commuter bus, would stop. Below, you can see two chimneys. That was Hilmo's house, which was right across from the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So you're pointing on the road that leads into Ahmici looking from above the mosque in the direction of the main road; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, from this vantage point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The school yard would be to the right and that would be the mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Still proceeding down the road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. Now we have passed this point here, and they are now at Redzo Pezer's house. I don't know. They must have filmed something or it is from an APC, and this is Redzo's house to the side. It's hard for me to explain exactly where I was at that time when they were around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Let's stop there for a moment, please. Do you see anything in the centre of the screen that can give you bearings and give us bearings as to where we are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. This is Fehima's house. It is this house here, and it is viewed from here. So this is where Redzo's house was, where this APC was. From there, you could see Fehima's house, and across from it, this was Hilmo's son, Fehim. In the distance, you can see the minaret which had fallen over the roof of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we continue, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is Fehima's stable which was behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What do you see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Can we back up a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we back up a little bit, please, to the previous shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No, no, no, just this. This may be enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us what we're looking at, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This big house is Hidajet's house which is located here. The fence remained intact throughout this period, and it still exists. It was running alongside the house. I am the boy who is lying down here on the grass in the dark clothing, and right now there's one UNPROFOR soldier there. Maybe you can see how he has split open the leg of my pants and he is dressing my wound, and you can see a portion of the skin, but it was just a cursory dressing that he gave me at that time. In the background, you can see Elvir's house and his barn with a white roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we continue, please, at normal speed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the two vehicles that came for me, and this is while they were working on my wound. While they were doing this, there was no interpreter there, there was no one there. So they asked me something, and as far as I could understand, which was just a few words, they asked me whether I was by myself and where I was, and they told me that they would take me to Zenica to the hospital. See, now I'm showing them that I was over there, that I was in this house here, that I had come to this place. Now the APCs went and turned around. Then I was put in the vehicle and I was taken to the hospital in Travnik. This is the road on which I had come. It's right here behind Hidajet's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Does that road look like that today or has it changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The road looks the same today. It is a dirt road and it is mixed in with gravel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Has it become somewhat overgrown, or do you know, from lack of use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. It was quite overgrown, but I believe that now it's been cleaned up and it looks as it used to look before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think the final series of questions, Mr. President, might be better done in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. President, before we proceed with the examination of the next witness, may I address the Court? A few minutes ago, in answer to your question, when I expressed the willingness of the Defence to accept the proposal of the Prosecution so as to make the best of the time available for hearing the witnesses, I said that I was speaking in my own name. However, my colleagues do not share my opinion. On the contrary, colleague Radovic and my learned friend Ms. Glumac are opposed to this, considering that we will be hearing witnesses in whose testimony they have a special interest. If we were to continue at this rate, which we, in principle, accept, they fear that they would not have enough time to prepare themselves properly for the cross-examination. Mr. President, may I make a further remark in this connection? At this point in time, I'm voicing the shared view of both the accused and their Defence, that there is no doubt that it is an imperative requirement for us to ensure a speedy, fair, and efficient trial. In this, we all agree. But we must point out that the rate at which we are going will not, we fear, contribute to the establishment of the facts. We, therefore, fear that it will not contribute to a fair trial. That is why we appeal to you to have understanding for this position of the accused and, of course, us as their representatives who have to be guided by their will. Your Honours, I felt it necessary to advise you of the common position of our clients and us as their Defence counsel. Thank you for having the patience to hear us out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We will stick to our timetable, and we will see as we go along how much time we need. In any case, your objections might relate to the new witness, the one mentioned by the Prosecutor, the lady who came here recently. But as for the other witnesses, you had the statements, and we will stick to our timetable. Of course, this means that you will have ample opportunity to cross-examine witnesses, but I think that we will try to have them called this week. We will see. In any case, tomorrow we will start at 9.30 and go on until 6.00 and the same applies to Friday. We will see how many witnesses we can hear here. Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This is Witness H?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Witness H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I shall ask Witness H to stand and to make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. I understand the protective measures include facial distortion and the pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. At this time, I will hand the usher a slip of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Witness H, I will inform you that you have requested protective measures and that they have been granted by the Court. So you may feel free and confident to provide evidence before this Tribunal. I will ask you a series of questions. If any of those questions would require an answer that might tend to reveal your identity, I will request the Court to go into closed session, which means your voice will not leave the room, and then you may feel free to provide full answers to those particular questions. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us, first, what year you were born in and how old you are now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: I was born in 1980 and, therefore, I'm 18 years old and six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How old were you in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: I was 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Where did you live at that time, what village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How long had you lived in Ahmici by April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Since my birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Without giving us the names of any members of your family right now, could you tell us what your family comprised of at that time, how many sisters, brothers, if you had any, father, mother, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: There were five of us. I had a mother and father and two sisters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask the usher to present an exhibit to the witness. Because this exhibit may reveal the identity, I would request a closed session while we talk about this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I understand we are now in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Whereupon hearing adjourned at 6.00 p.m. to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of September, 1998 at 9.30 a.m.
